chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah said: He narrated to me Mu'adh ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Do not leave out reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' in seven stations: in the two rak'ahs before Fajr, the two rak'ahs of Zawal, the two rak'ahs after Maghrib, the two rak'ahs at the beginning of the Night Prayer, the two rak'ahs of Ihram and Fajr when you wake up with them, and the two rak'ahs of Tawaf.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْإِحْرَامِ: Rak'ata al-Ihram (The two rak'ahs of entry into prayer)

ai.seo_question: Which two Quranic chapters should be recited in specific voluntary prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the spiritual potency of reciting Al-Ikhlas and Al-Kafirun as acts of devotion and theological affirmation in seven specific prayer units, including the Sunnah of Fajr and the two Rak'ahs of Tawaf. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating concise, high-impact Quranic recitations into daily ritual life to reinforce monotheism and distinctiveness from other faiths. The selection of these stations highlights the continuity of prophetic tradition in maintaining spiritual vigilance through structured, repeated remembrance.
